## What you take with you {.smaller}

::: {.small}
- A reproduction of one of the five reanalyses, to the third decimal, run in R and written into a report
- The data-management checks that would have caught the slips of three of the five pipelines
- A working knowledge of the toolchain: R, an IDE, Quarto, git and the places where finished work is deposited
- For reading: the case study on the course site, the companion modules on R, the IDE, Quarto, Git and GitHub, data sources and repositories, and the three *Nature* papers of 2026 [@MiskeEtAl2026InvestigatingReproducibilitySocial; @AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness; @TynerEtAl2026InvestigatingReplicabilitySocial]
- For later: the research-software and open-research teams at your university, and a ReproducibiliTea journal club near you
:::

::: {.urlbox}
{{< var site-url >}}

::: notes
You take home a reproduction of one of the five analyses, run in R and written into a report, the checks that would have caught three slips in five pipelines, and a working knowledge of the tools that make an analysis something that another person can rerun. The companion modules on the course site take each tool further, at your own pace: R, the IDE, Quarto, Git and GitHub, where data come from, and where finished work is deposited. Two pointers for keeping the habit alive. Most universities have a research-software engineering team and an open-research or library data service that run training like today's, and ReproducibiliTea journal clubs meet in dozens of cities. If there is none near you, they will help you start one.
:::
